claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was a Christian monk and ascetic who lived from 345 to 399 AD.
Evagrius was born in Ibora in Pontus and died in Cellia in the Nitrian Desert, Egypt.
Evagrius left Constantinople around 382 and became a monk in Jerusalem in 383 at the monastery of Rufinus and Melania the Elder, then moved to Egypt where he spent the rest of his life.
The Praktikos was originally written in Greek.
The Praktikos is a guide to ascetic life.
The Praktikos was addressed to Anatolius, as indicated in the prologue where Evagrius responds to a letter from Anatolius written from the Holy Mountain while Evagrius was in Scetis.
Evagrius wrote the Praktikos to explain the ascetic life, dividing it into 100 chapters on practical matters and indicating a further work of 650 chapters on knowledge (the Gnostikos).
The Praktikos is the best preserved of all Evagrian writings due to the relatively large number of manuscripts and wide distribution.
Manuscripts of the Praktikos exist in Syriac, Armenian, Ethiopic (Ge'ez), Georgian, and Arabic.
Demons are mentioned in 67 of the 100 chapters of the Praktikos.
